summary: Iter 375 — Verified Wayly parity batch across backend (notification auto-prune + regression) and both frontends (mobile Expo web preview + web). All testable acceptance items PASS. 2/2 pytest tests pass. Backend: GET /api/notifications prunes a seeded TEST_STALE notification whose link points to a non-existent statement id (/app/statements/<bogus-id>) AND confirms the row is deleted from Mongo (second fetch stays empty), while a sibling list-link notification (/app/statements) is retained. POST /notifications/read and GET/PUT /notifications/prefs still work (round-trip of a flipped pref returns the new value then restores). Mobile (Expo preview @ 390x844): login screen tagline 'AGED CARE, MADE CLEAR' renders on EXACTLY 1 line (lineHeight=32, height=32, fontSize=26); login with cathy@example.com succeeds; dashboard shows Wayly wordmark + shaded teal header, serif teal greeting 'Good morning, Cathy.', 'Viewing care for Mum' teal pill (testID dashboard-viewing-for) under greeting, bottom tab bar Dashboard/Tools/Statements/More all rendered and visible, NO hamburger icon top-right (bell + avatar only). ThemeProvider default pref='light' (confirmed in src/theme/ThemeContext.tsx line 24). Web: dashboard greeting is serif teal with 'Viewing care for Dorothy Smith' pill (dashboard-viewing-for) — no regression. Authenticated 404: visiting /app/this-does-not-exist-xyz while logged in shows the friendly in-app card (notfound-inapp present, notfound-dashboard present) and the public marketing 404 (notfound-home) is NOT rendered. Code review confirms NotificationsBell.safePath guard (lines 14-16, 71, 134, 238-250) makes non-navigable links render as a button instead of a Link, so a stale/odd link never dumps the user on the 404 page. Google native Android sign-in NOT tested per request (requires published build).

critical_code_review_comments: backend/routes/notifications.py _prune_stale_notifications: parses target collection for statements/invoices/reports only. Any future deep-link resource type (e.g. letters, care-plans) added to notifications will not be auto-pruned until added here. Document the whitelist (STATEMENT_SUBPAGES set + the two hardcoded prefixes) or make it config-driven.

notifications prune runs on every GET /api/notifications (potentially 30 docs × up-to-3 collection lookups). Current scale is fine. If notifications grow or multi-tab polling becomes aggressive, batch the three $in queries behind a single asyncio.gather for parallelism (already set up to do by-collection grouping).

frontend NotificationsBell.jsx: safePath only accepts strings starting with '/'. External/absolute 'https://…' notifications would render as non-navigating buttons — correct behavior for safety, but if the product ever intends to deep-link to an external URL (e.g. ACQSC guidance), this guard will swallow it silently.
test_credentials: cathy@example.com / testpass123 (family caregiver). Dorothy Smith is the active participant on web; 'Mum' is the active participant label on mobile — both are the same account, likely different participant_switcher states (not a bug, just a seed difference between surfaces).

Mobile Expo preview auth works via normal login flow (no AsyncStorage shim needed for login screen tests); for post-login screens on web preview you can continue using the two-key AsyncStorage pattern noted in iter374. rca of the issue: N/A — all acceptance items pass. The notification auto-prune implementation in /app/backend/routes/notifications.py (_parse_notification_target + _prune_stale_notifications) correctly: (1) only extracts a (collection, resource_id) tuple when the link is /app/statements/<id> (and <id> not in {upload, archived}), /app/invoices/<id>, or /app/reports?report_id=<id> — so list pages like /app/statements, /app/budget-alerts, /settings/notifications fall through and are kept; (2) does one $in lookup per collection to decide which resource ids still exist; (3) delete_many's the stale notification ids under the current user_id and returns the surviving items. Unread count is recomputed by a count_documents call AFTER the prune, so the badge stays accurate. The mobile dashboard parity work (WaylyHeader + teal→clay gradient, no hamburger, serif greeting, dashboard-viewing-for pill, bottom tab bar) matches the web reference. The ThemeContext default of 'light' + 'storage.getItem is only applied if saved' guarantees fresh loads start in light mode without preventing the Settings → theme switcher from working.
